standard.title: Name letters and common sounds
standard.description: recognise and name all upper- and lower-case letters (graphemes) and know the most common sound that each letter represents
standard.prior_knowledge: Students may recognise letters in their own name and in familiar texts. They have not yet been explicitly taught all upper- and lower-case letter names and their most common associated sounds.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can recognise and name all upper- and lower-case letters and identify the most common sound each letter represents — demonstrating complete alphabet knowledge across both cases.

nodes.label: Letters have names
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise and name most upper- and lower-case letters when shown them.
nodes.minimum_width: Recognise and name at least fifteen lower-case letters.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise and name all upper- and lower-case letters; match upper- and lower-case pairs; apply letter naming in the context of familiar words and texts.
wider: Recognise letters across a range of fonts and handwriting styles — understanding that the same letter takes different visual forms
Identify letters in environmental print, books, signs and digital texts — building multi-context letter recognition
Compare the English alphabet with other alphabetic writing systems — noting similarities and differences
nodes.hinge_reason: Letter name knowledge is a prerequisite for letter-sound learning in Node 2 — without reliable letter identification, students cannot associate sounds with specific letters, and phonics instruction cannot proceed effectively.

response_modes.reason: Complete and automatic letter name knowledge is a prerequisite for phonics instruction — uncertain letter names slow decoding and letter-sound learning. Practice to automaticity is required.

success_criteria: Student can name all twenty-six upper-case letters.
Student can name all twenty-six lower-case letters.
Student can match upper- and lower-case letter pairs.

nodes.label: Letters represent sounds
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the most common sound represented by each letter.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce the most common sound for at least fifteen letters.
nodes.typical_width: Know the most common sound each letter represents; connect letter names to letter sounds; apply letter-sound knowledge in the context of simple reading and spelling.
wider: Identify the most common sound for all twenty-six letters, then explore that some letters have more than one common sound (e.g. 'c' in 'cat' vs 'city')
Connect letter-sound knowledge to words encountered in reading — applying the knowledge in context rather than isolation
Explore sounds in other languages — noting that the same letter may represent different sounds in different languages
nodes.hinge_reason: Letter-sound associations are the prerequisite for all phonic decoding in LY04, LY12 and LY13 — without automatic letter-to-sound retrieval, students cannot blend or segment, and reading and spelling both fail at the letter level.

response_modes.reason: Letter-sound associations require practice to automaticity — slow retrieval directly limits decoding speed. The 'most common sound' must be the automatic first response before alternative sounds are introduced.

success_criteria: Student can produce the most common sound for each letter of the alphabet.
Student can connect a letter to its sound when prompted by either the letter name or the letter form.
